First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨-\frac{4}{{t}^{3/2}}\,,\frac{4}{t+1}⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨-\frac{4}{{t}^{3/2}}\,,\frac{4}{t+1}⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int -\frac{4}{{t}^{3/2}}\,\text{d}t,\int \frac{4}{t+1}\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}+{c}_{1},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(1)=⟨2,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1)=⟨\frac{8}{\sqrt{1}}+{c}_{1},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)⟩ \\ ⟨8+{c}_{1},\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨2,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(2)⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=-6$ and ${c}_{2}=0.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨\frac{8}{\sqrt{t}}-6,\,4\operatorname{ln}⁡(t+1)⟩.
$$
